title: Reconcile hibernation resume parameters with the swapfile
head: b104761b313d

leads.summary: First-time mapping failure publishes a success marker and is treated as a completed setup
leads.consequence: When btrfs map-swapfile fails or outputs invalid data on a first run, reconcile returns failure, but the caller only warns, writes HOOKS+=(resume), rebuilds unless --no-rebuild, and can return 0 without resume.conf. The factory-reset caller checks exit status and existence of the swapfile, so it proceeds to rebuild boot files even though hibernation cannot resume. The availability predicate tests swap size plus the marker, not resume.conf. A later setup can repair it if mapping recovers, but no automatic retry occurs.
leads.triage: dropped; first-time warn-and-continue is the intended installer/factory-reset behaviour, confirmed by Opus; later setup repairs

leads.summary: A successful limine-mkinitcpio exit does not prove the edited resume parameters reached all boot entries
leads.consequence: On a per-kernel mkinitcpio or image-build failure, upstream reports the failure but returns success for that kernel and the outer loop ignores the return code. The new script sees success, retains the changed resume.conf and prints 'already set up'. Future reruns see identical text and never retry; one or all old UKIs may still contain the previous offset, risking a cold boot rather than resume. Verify the UKI/entry for each installed kernel after rebuilding or ensure the build tool reports and propagates individual failures; do not rely on exit status alone. No native boot image generation was performed.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus F1; same mechanism, already in Opus final

leads.summary: Removing hibernation leaves the generated resume.conf and rebuilds boot files with stale resume parameters
leads.consequence: After setup writes or refreshes resume.conf, 'omarchy hibernation remove' removes its swapfile and hook but not resume.conf, then invokes limine-mkinitcpio, so the next boot still has resume=/dev/... resume_offset=... pointing at the removed swapfile. This pre-exists the PR but is a lifecycle gap for the config now actively reconciled. Related open #13584 and #13768 both add deletion on removal; if one merges, the omission is fixed. No actual boot or hibernation was run.
leads.triage: dropped; pre-existing hibernation-remove gap; covered by related open PRs #13768/#13584

leads.summary: Mount SOURCE need not be the physical device containing a multi-device Btrfs swapfile
leads.consequence: On a Btrfs filesystem with more than one device where all swapfile extents reside on the device other than the mount's reported SOURCE, map-swapfile -r returns a physical offset of the actual stripe but findmnt reports the mount source. The generated resume=<mount source> and resume_offset=<actual stripe offset> can be well-formed yet refer to different devices, silently making resume fail. Source establishes both outputs are independent; a real multi-device fixture pairing SOURCE and stripe device, or a kernel hibernation test, would confirm occurrence on the target distro. Keep as hypothesis until then.
leads.triage: dropped; hypothesis only (multi-device Btrfs); same findmnt derivation as before the PR

leads.summary: The new tests cannot catch wrong findmnt or btrfs operands
leads.consequence: findmnt ignores all its arguments; the btrfs stub returns the same numeric offset for every invocation. A plausible regression to findmnt -T / or mapping a different swapfile would still yield the same asserted resume.conf in this fixture; on a separate /swap mount it could configure the wrong resume device. Make both stubs check exact command, flags and $SWAP_FILE, and add a negative case for wrong operands. The test does exercise changed and unchanged offsets but not the command target.
leads.triage: dropped; generic stub hardening with no demonstrated surviving mutant

leads.summary: Open #5761 cannot be merged mechanically with this PR's resume-marker paths
leads.consequence: #5761 changes the authoritative hook marker to /etc/mkinitcpio.conf.d/omarchy_hooks.conf, removes the old omarchy_resume.conf and changes hibernation-available accordingly. The real merge-file with that PR's own base produces two conflicts in setup. If a manual conflict resolution retains this PR's old marker writer but #5761's new availability/removal consumers, setup can say configured while Hibernate is hidden and removal cannot find its marker. Resolve all three scripts, migration and first-run/re-entry tests together; this is a confirmed integration conflict, not a claim that GitHub will merge this specific bad resolution.
leads.triage: verified by coordinator (gh pr view/diff 5761), published as Details note; #5761 open, base dev, CONFLICTING, moves hook to omarchy_hooks.conf and deletes omarchy_resume.conf

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** A failed image build is reported as success and never retried, keeping the stale `resume_offset` in the boot image.

### Skipped image builds are not retried

The rollback runs only on a nonzero exit, but `limine-mkinitcpio` logs `mkinitcpio failed for kernel X, skipping.` and exits 0. **Impact:** setup reports success, reruns skip the rebuild, and resume cold-boots (#11437) until another rebuild.

**Suggested change (untested):** Treat a rebuilt UKI whose `.cmdline` lacks the new `resume_offset` as a failed rebuild (see Details).

<details><summary>Reproducer (fails at b104761b)</summary>

### Reproducer: a failed image build is reported as success and never retried

The rollback in the already-configured path only runs when `sudo limine-mkinitcpio` exits nonzero. Upstream `limine-mkinitcpio` (limine-entry-tool, the version Omarchy packages, 1.40.0, and 1.38.0 from #11437) logs a failed image build and continues with exit status 0. In `install/arch-linux/limine-mkinitcpio-hook/usr/share/libalpm/scripts/limine-mkinitcpio-install` at tag 1.40.0:

- line 230: `error_msg "mkinitcpio failed for kernel ${KERNEL_VERSION}, skipping."` then `return 1`
- line 234: the `install_uki` result (copying the image to the ESP) is not checked
- line 297: `process_uki_kernel || return 0`
- line 315: `process_kernel "$kernel_dir" || true`

Build and ESP-install failures never make it exit nonzero; nonzero exits come from setup errors, the boot hooks (`exit 2` at line 310, `exit 3` at line 320), finding no kernel (line 305) and the removed-kernel cleanup (lines 324-327). `migrations/1789325478.sh` line 34 in this repository says the same thing: "limine-mkinitcpio can return success after skipping a failed kernel build."

The test below uses the harness from `test/shell.d/hibernation-resume-reconcile-test.sh`. Its `limine-mkinitcpio` stub prints the same error line as upstream and returns 0. It records the drop-in as the "boot image" only when the build works. Save it as `test/shell.d/hibernation-skipped-build-test.sh` in a checkout of the PR head:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Reproducer: limine-mkinitcpio exits 0 after skipping a kernel whose image
# build failed (limine-mkinitcpio-install: "mkinitcpio failed for kernel X,
# skipping." then `process_uki_kernel || return 0` and
# `process_kernel ... || true`). The stub below does the same. The new drop-in
# stays, setup reports success, and a later run never rebuilds the image.
# Harness copied from test/shell.d/hibernation-resume-reconcile-test.sh.
set -euo pipefail
source "$(dirname "$0")/base-test.sh"

test_tmp=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$test_tmp"' EXIT
export test_tmp
printf 'HOOKS+=(resume)\n' >"$test_tmp/mkinitcpio.conf"
touch "$test_tmp/image_size" "$test_tmp/swapfile"
sed '/^if ! $FORCE; then/,$d' "$ROOT/bin/omarchy-hibernation-setup" |
  sed -e "s|/sys/power/image_size|$test_tmp/image_size|g" \
    -e "s|/etc/mkinitcpio.conf.d/omarchy_resume.conf|$test_tmp/mkinitcpio.conf|g" \
    -e "s|/etc/limine-entry-tool.d/resume.conf|$test_tmp/resume.conf|g" \
    -e "s|/swap/swapfile|$test_tmp/swapfile|g" >"$test_tmp/setup"

sudo() {
  case "$1" in
    btrfs) printf '%s\n' "${TEST_OFFSET:-456}" ;;
    limine-mkinitcpio)
      echo rebuild >>"$test_tmp/rebuilds"
      if [[ -n ${TEST_BUILD_FAILS:-} ]]; then
        echo "ERROR: mkinitcpio failed for kernel 7.2.5-3-omarchy, skipping." >&2
      else
        cp "$test_tmp/resume.conf" "$test_tmp/image-cmdline"
      fi
      return 0
      ;;
    /usr/bin/install) cp -- "${@: -2}" ;;
    *) "$@" ;;
  esac
}
findmnt() { printf '%s\n' '/dev/mapper/root[/@]'; }
omarchy-cmd-missing() { return 1; }
export -f sudo findmnt omarchy-cmd-missing

# The boot image was built from the old drop-in.
printf 'KERNEL_CMDLINE[default]+=" resume=/dev/mapper/root resume_offset=123"\n' >"$test_tmp/resume.conf"
cp "$test_tmp/resume.conf" "$test_tmp/image-cmdline"

# The swapfile moved to 456 and the image build fails.
status=0
TEST_BUILD_FAILS=1 bash "$test_tmp/setup" >"$test_tmp/output" 2>&1 || status=$?
printf 'first run (build fails): exit %s\n' "$status"
sed 's/^/  /' "$test_tmp/output"

# After the build error is fixed, setup is run again.
bash "$test_tmp/setup" >"$test_tmp/output" 2>&1
printf 'second run (build works): exit 0\n'
sed 's/^/  /' "$test_tmp/output"
printf 'rebuild attempts: %s\n' "$(wc -l <"$test_tmp/rebuilds")"
printf 'drop-in:      %s\n' "$(<"$test_tmp/resume.conf")"
printf 'boot image:   %s\n' "$(<"$test_tmp/image-cmdline")"

cmp -s "$test_tmp/resume.conf" "$test_tmp/image-cmdline" ||
  fail "a later setup rebuilds the boot image that still has the old offset"
pass "a skipped image build is retried"
```

Run from the repository root:

```
bash test/shell.d/hibernation-skipped-build-test.sh
```

Actual output at b104761b (exit status 1):

```
first run (build fails): exit 0
  Updated resume parameters for /tmp/tmp.YsfhidQEtQ/swapfile
  ERROR: mkinitcpio failed for kernel 7.2.5-3-omarchy, skipping.
  Hibernation is already set up
second run (build works): exit 0
  Hibernation is already set up
rebuild attempts: 1
drop-in:      KERNEL_CMDLINE[default]+=" resume=/dev/mapper/root resume_offset=456"
boot image:   KERNEL_CMDLINE[default]+=" resume=/dev/mapper/root resume_offset=123"
not ok - a later setup rebuilds the boot image that still has the old offset
```

The stub's exit status matches upstream: the real `limine-mkinitcpio-install` control flow (1.38.0 and 1.40.0), run with a `mkinitcpio` that fails for the only kernel, exited 0 and added no boot entry.
</details>

### v3.4.0/v3.4.1 drop-ins are refused as custom

They wrote no space after `+="`; the ownership regex (line 85) requires one. **Impact:** setup exits 1 asking for a manual update, so #11437 stays unfixed there and a previously repaired empty offset now fails.

**Suggested change:** Use `\+=\"[[:space:]]?resume=` to make the space optional.

<details><summary>Reproducer (fails at b104761b)</summary>

### Reproducer: a resume.conf written by Omarchy v3.4.0 or v3.4.1 is refused as custom

Omarchy v3.4.0 and v3.4.1 wrote the drop-in as `KERNEL_CMDLINE[default]+="resume=$RESUME_DEVICE resume_offset=$RESUME_OFFSET"`, with no space after the opening quote (`git show v3.4.0:bin/omarchy-hibernation-setup`, line 78; the space was added in v3.4.2 by e1ee8e85 "Fix smushing"). Those releases also ran `btrfs inspect-internal map-swapfile` without `sudo` (fixed in v3.5.0 by 4c5e6569), which can leave the offset empty. Before this PR, the `resume_offset="$` repair handled that empty offset. At b104761b the ownership regex requires whitespace after the quote, so setup exits 1 instead.

Add this case to `test/shell.d/hibernation-resume-reconcile-test.sh` after line 66 (`pass "empty device or offset from an earlier setup is repaired"`):

```bash

# Omarchy 3.4.0 and 3.4.1 wrote this line without the space after the quote.
printf 'KERNEL_CMDLINE[default]+="resume=/dev/mapper/root resume_offset="\n' >"$test_tmp/resume.conf"
bash "$test_tmp/setup" --no-rebuild >"$test_tmp/output" 2>&1 || fail "setup repairs a 3.4.0 drop-in" "$(<"$test_tmp/output")"
grep -Fqx 'KERNEL_CMDLINE[default]+=" resume=/dev/mapper/root resume_offset=456"' "$test_tmp/resume.conf" || fail "the 3.4.0 drop-in is replaced"
pass "drop-ins written by Omarchy 3.4.0 and 3.4.1 are repaired"
```

Run from the repository root:

```
bash test/shell.d/hibernation-resume-reconcile-test.sh
```

Actual output at b104761b (exit status 1):

```
ok - existing hibernation follows a relocated swapfile and rebuilds
ok - reconciliation is idempotent
ok - no-rebuild repairs parameters without rebuilding
ok - invalid mappings fail without replacing boot configuration
ok - custom drop-ins are preserved
ok - empty device or offset from an earlier setup is repaired
Custom resume configuration in /tmp/tmp.JtGhl1N9FC/resume.conf; update its resume parameters manually.
not ok - setup repairs a 3.4.0 drop-in
```

With the space made optional on line 85 of `bin/omarchy-hibernation-setup`:

```diff
-    if [[ ! $current =~ ^KERNEL_CMDLINE\[default\]\+=\"[[:space:]]resume=[^\"[:space:]]*[[:space:]]resume_offset=[0-9]*\"$ ]]; then
+    if [[ ! $current =~ ^KERNEL_CMDLINE\[default\]\+=\"[[:space:]]?resume=[^\"[:space:]]*[[:space:]]resume_offset=[0-9]*\"$ ]]; then
```

the same file passes (exit status 0):

```
ok - existing hibernation follows a relocated swapfile and rebuilds
ok - reconciliation is idempotent
ok - no-rebuild repairs parameters without rebuilding
ok - invalid mappings fail without replacing boot configuration
ok - custom drop-ins are preserved
ok - empty device or offset from an earlier setup is repaired
ok - drop-ins written by Omarchy 3.4.0 and 3.4.1 are repaired
ok - missing drop-ins are repaired and failed rebuilds remain retryable
ok - existing parameters survive failed rebuilds and retries rebuild again
ok - first-time setup writes resume parameters
ok - first-time setup warns on an unreadable mapping and a later setup repairs it
```

The same refusal applies to a v3.4.0/v3.4.1 line with a stale non-empty offset, which is the #11437 case on those systems. With a standalone copy of the same harness (its own test label) and `printf 'KERNEL_CMDLINE[default]+="resume=/dev/mapper/root resume_offset=123"\n' >"$test_tmp/resume.conf"` followed by `bash "$test_tmp/setup" --no-rebuild`, the actual output at b104761b is (exit status 1):

```
Custom resume configuration in /tmp/tmp.pBXl8tuQ0c/resume.conf; update its resume parameters manually.
not ok - setup repairs a stale offset in a v3.4.0 drop-in
```
</details>

<details><summary>Details</summary>

**Verified:**
- The new test passes 10/10 at the head and fails its first assertion against the merge-base script.
- A rerun rewrites a stale device or offset once; a second run changes nothing.
- `resume= resume_offset=N` (#12630) and an empty offset in the current format are repaired; extra lines are preserved as custom.
- First-time `--force --no-rebuild` (installer, factory reset) warns instead of failing on an unreadable mapping.
- `map-swapfile -r` prints the offset in page units, which is what the kernel's `resume_offset=` expects.

**Exit status:** `migrations/1789325478.sh` already notes that `limine-mkinitcpio` can return success after skipping a failed kernel build.

**Suggested change, detail:** `omarchy-upgrade-to-quattro` (lines 623-630) already reads a UKI `.cmdline` for `root=`. UKIs built with `--no-cmdline` (sbctl Secure Boot with Snapper) have none, so that case needs the `/boot/limine.conf` cmdline instead.

**Related open PRs:** #13768, #13908 and #9860 (base `quattro`) edit the same block of `omarchy-hibernation-setup`. #5761 (base `dev`, already conflicting) moves the resume hook into `omarchy_hooks.conf` and deletes `omarchy_resume.conf`, the marker this PR checks.
</details>
